Topic 5.1: Book keeping (Importance of bookkeeping, preparing simple financial statements for a business, financial records
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Book keeping (Importance of bookkeeping, preparing simple financial statements for a business, financial records, part of Entrepreneurship in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is bookkeeping important to a business? 2. How are the statements of financial position, cash flow and income prepared?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Book keeping (Importance of bookkeeping, preparing simple financial statements for a business, financial records together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: The learner acquires skills of organising, self-learning and works collaboratively when preparing

statements of financial position, cash flow and income.

● Critical thinking and problem-solving: The learner acquires evaluation and decision-making skills when calculating

assets, liabilities and capital using the bookkeeping equation.

● Communication and collaboration: The learner develops writing, speaking, listening, reading and teamwork skills when

discussing, brainstorming and presenting on the components of statement of financial position, cash flows and income.

● Self-efficacy: The learner develops effective communication skills when discussing, presenting and preparing statements of

financial position, cash flow and income.

Values:
● Peace: The learner works harmoniously with members of the team when brainstorming and presenting the meaning, basic

terms and importance of bookkeeping for a business in learning activities.

● Responsibility: The learner shows hard work as they perform tasks assigned when discussing the components of a

statement of financial position, cash flows and income statement.

● Respect: The learner shows regard for the input of every member of the team when discussing the components of a

statement of financial position, cash flow and income statement.

68

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Financial literacy: The learner enhances bookkeeping skills when drawing and presenting simple statements of financial

position, cash flow and income for a business.

● Career Guidance: The learner identifies career opportunities when brainstorming and presenting basic terms and

importance of bookkeeping for a business.

Link to other subjects:

● Mathematics: The learner relates mathematical formulas while calculating assets, liabilities and capital using the

bookkeeping equation.

● Kenyan sign language: The learners apply the signing skills as they fingerspell and sign terms related to bookkeeping as

a learning area.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Print and non-print media

• Digital devices

• Sample financial statements,

• Sample financial records
